layers.face: The stable at Maplegate is his, and has been for thirty years. In his fifties, he barely speaks — a day’s words might not run past twenty, and each one lands. The day you arrived he carried your bag and drove the cart, said nothing the whole way, and at the door left you three words, Martha’s inside, before leading the horse off.
layers.inside: He has been here longer than anyone, and remembers every master and steward the estate has turned over. His loyalty is not to whoever holds the estate but to the stable and this land — grown out of thirty years of work, not written into a contract. Ten kind words will not earn his trust; a mended stable roof will. The horse the last steward left behind — he knows something of it.
layers.archetype: A Valewisp groom is an old kind of post: not quite a servant, not quite hired labour, more a sinew between the estate and its land. Rational feudalism writes each person’s place into a contract; a man like him is the order that gathers outside it, out of years and craft. The morning you come for your horse and find it already set right, the tack on the near hook, no word said — that is him counting you as one of his own.

marta.title: Martha
marta.subtitle: Head of the kitchen
marta.silhouette: The one who runs the kitchen

layers.face: The kitchen is hers, and there is always flour on the apron. In her forties, a big voice and a bigger laugh, plain and direct; you were looked over head to foot the moment you came in.
layers.inside: Nothing on the estate moves without her knowing it — who is at odds with whom, where the accounts run thin. Whether she says so depends on whether you ask, and whether it is worth the telling. The big voice makes her seem unable to keep a thing, which is its own cover: she always says less than she knows.
layers.archetype: On a Valewisp estate the head of the kitchen is often the house’s real hub: masters come and go, the hearth stays lit. The whole of the duchy’s dignity rests on hospitality, and the one who can read a table — what to serve, and when — holds not authority but news, and goodwill. The day she remembers what you will not eat and quietly cooks to your taste, saying nothing of it, that is her way.

layers.face: The maid of the main house — cleaning, laundry, and the tidying of the office besides. Quiet, sparing with words; she barely spoke showing you up to the room, but the eyes are sharp.
layers.inside: Because the rooms and the papers on the desks all pass under her hands, more reaches her than anyone credits a maid with seeing. She knows more than she lets on. That faded rectangle on your desk — she would know what used to stand there.
layers.archetype: Whoever tends the rooms is the estate’s quietest archive — rational feudalism sets everything down on paper, and the one who dusts the paper sees the whole house without being seen.

layers.face: The master of the Maplegate forge-chapel, who serves Thornwall and Millridge besides. Past fifty. In the Temple Forged by the Sacred Flame the clergy are craftsmen, not pastors; what he keeps is the fire in the hearth, not a pulpit.
layers.inside: He keeps the vigil at the forge-chapel on Thursdays. He presses no belief on anyone; he simply treats the fire as a thing that ought to be tended. Weddings, funerals, a quarrel between neighbours — people tend to bring them to him first. He could have stayed at the capital’s sanctum and climbed; in the end he chose to come back.
layers.archetype: In Valewisp faith is closer to respect for the natural order than to doctrine. The master is what that local faith looks like: at the kingdom’s centre the institution is a sanctum and a minting seal; here it is one man keeping a fire. When a life ends here, it is he who returns it to the flame. He knows a great deal, and volunteers none of it.

layers.face: The lady of Thornwall. In her sixties, silver hair kept without a strand loose. You will most likely meet her at the hunt or a dinner — she need not raise her voice to still a room.
layers.inside: Valehold fashion, which household is due a call, which dinner cannot be missed — she has it all straight. She is measured with people, and she remembers a kindness. Her word carries weight: a person she will vouch for needs little other proof.
layers.archetype: The baroness is a hub of Valewisp’s noble society and its quiet arbiter — to miss the hunt is to say something is wrong, and it is usually the lady of the house who arranges these occasions. She has lived in the valley long enough to have watched two generations of it change, and to know that each year’s fire is not the same fire.

layers.face: The Baron of Millridge, a little past forty. Always smiling, always proposing something — it was his letter that drew you into the hunt. His warmth is easy as sunlight, and does not quite outlast his turning away.
layers.inside: He cares more for the woods, the hunting ground and appearances, and is the most active host of the season — a farther stag, a new trail, another dish at dinner — the talk threaded with small arrangements made in the gaps. Whether an invitation from him is a welcome or a way to keep the new steward where he can be watched is a fair thing to weigh.
layers.archetype: He is the kind of baron who is perfectly fluent in the web of contract and turns it to his own account without once breaking a rule — harder to deal with than a man who breaks them, because you cannot quite tell him from the system itself. Every noble here owes duties upward and a guarantee downward, the way Baron von Alde stood surety for you; Henk only reads that ledger of obligations closer than most.

rational_feudalism.title: Rational Feudalism
rational_feudalism.subtitle: Kingdom of Marigni
rational_feudalism.text: What sets the Kingdom of Marigni apart: monarch, council and parliament coexist, and feudal contracts run inside a modern legal frame. It is ancient, restrained, intensely private, its politics unbroken since medieval times. The currency is the Guldmark. The guarantee letter between you and Baron von Alde is this system in its everyday form — favour and law in force at once.

sacred_flame.title: Temple Forged by the Sacred Flame
sacred_flame.subtitle: Marigni’s faith
sacred_flame.text: It venerates the Sacred Fire and the act of forging — the self as raw iron to be shaped. Its clergy are masters and forge-keepers, not pastors; a place of worship has a hearth, not an altar, the fire set into the floor at the centre. At the kingdom’s heart it is institution — sanctum, minting seal, the authentication of contracts; here in Valewisp it is closer to respect for the seasons and the natural order.

valewisp_duchy.title: Valewisp
valewisp_duchy.subtitle: The river duchy
valewisp_duchy.silhouette: The duchy you are bound for
valewisp_duchy.text: Marigni’s largest duchy — a temperate valley, rich farmland, mixed woods. Its economy is grain, timber, livestock, a little wine. It prizes courtesy, bloodline and the rhythm of the seasons — to be hasty is an insult, to be idle no more forgivable; time runs by season, not by clock. It thinks itself the most noble of the duchies: not from arrogance, but from living closest to the order of the land.

maplegate.title: Maplegate
maplegate.subtitle: North of Valehold
maplegate.silhouette: The estate you are to keep
maplegate.text: A middling estate in the district north of Valehold, Baron von Alde’s holding. Stone walls, timber tiles, an avenue of maples burning with autumn. The last steward left suddenly, with no handover at all; the harvest is near and the estate’s work has stood three weeks. You have thirty days.

millridge.title: Millridge
millridge.text: An estate in the valley. You have heard the name, and no more than that.
